13 The diagram represents a sphere under water. P, Q, R and S are forces acting on the sphere due
to the pressure of the water.
water surface
P
Q
S
R
Each force acts perpendicularly to the sphere’s surface. P and R act in opposite directions
vertically. Q and S act in opposite directions horizontally.
Which information about the magnitudes of the forces is correct?
A
P < R and S = Q
B
P > R and S = Q
C
P = R and S = Q and P < S
D
P = R and S = Q and P = S

hints: Notice where P and R act: P pushes down on the top of the sphere and R pushes up on the bottom, so compare their depths below the water surface.
Recall that liquid pressure increases with depth as $p = h\rho g$, and force on a given area is $F = pA$, so link greater depth to greater force.
Check Q and S: both push horizontally at the centre level of the sphere, so ask whether depth and pressure are different for that left-right pair.
walkthrough: Identify the positions: P is on the top of the sphere at a smaller depth, R is on the bottom at a larger depth, while Q and S act on opposite sides at the same vertical level.
State the governing rule: in a liquid of density $\rho$, pressure at depth $h$ is $p = h\rho g$, so pressure is greater deeper down.
Apply $F = pA$ to the vertical pair: the effective area is the same, but $h$ for R is larger than $h$ for P, so $p$ below is larger and hence $R > P$, or $P < R$.
Apply the same rule to the horizontal pair: Q and S are at the same depth $h$, so $p$ is the same on left and right and the opposite forces cancel, giving $S = Q$.
Combine the results as $P < R$ and $S = Q$. This is option A.

A.explanation: R is at greater depth than P so water pressure and force is larger below, while Q and S are at the same depth so their forces balance.

B.explanation: Pressure increases with depth, so the upward force R from below cannot be smaller than the downward force P from above.

C.explanation: Q and S are equal but P cannot equal R because the top and bottom of the sphere are at different depths in the water.

D.explanation: Equal forces in all directions would need equal pressure all round, which is false because pressure depends on depth below the water surface.
